failures.criterion: A code path whose first run is after the merge is executed before the merge (skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md, 'The rules every phase's evidence follows'): the worker image's registry cache write
failures.evidence: worker-image.yaml:171-172 moves the build cache to ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker:buildcache, with `cache-to: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && format('type=registry,ref={0}:buildcache,mode=max', env.IMAGE) || '' }}`. So the export runs for the first time in release.yaml's worker image build on main, after the merge. BuildKit fails the build when a cache export fails (no ignore-error is set), so a failure there stops main's release worker image. No proof exercises the write. Every pull-request build so far only read the cache: scratch #2352's worker-image / build (job 122047998245) logs '#13 importing cache manifest from ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker:buildcache' then 'ERROR: failed to configure registry cache importer: ... buildcache: not found', and the build passes. That proves a missing cache is tolerated, and nothing about the write. The productionCheck entry 'main's two release worker builds both completing' reads it only after main has run it. I tried to run the probe myself: a scratch branch on legion/INFRA-520 that sets cache-from and cache-to to `type=registry,ref=${{ env.IMAGE }}:buildcache-infra520-tester[,mode=max]`. GitHub refused the push: 'refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow .github/workflows/worker-image.yaml without workflows permission'. The review App lacks the workflows permission, and the implement App has it. Fix: the implementer pushes that scratch branch as a stacked scratch pull request, which selects only worker-image (and lint). It reads the worker-image / build log for 'exporting cache to registry' / 'writing cache manifest ... buildcache-infra520-tester' and a successful step. It re-runs that job once and shows 'importing cache manifest from ...buildcache-infra520-tester' with CACHED layers. Then it closes the pull request and records both runs as a proof entry (the negative control is the not-found import above). No repository test can pin this: it is a registry write that only a run performs. Out of scope: the Go cache saves on push (actions/cache/save 55cc8345 src/saveImpl.ts:75-77 turns every save error, an empty key included, into a warning, so they cannot fail a main run), and docs-deploy (the same upload-pages-artifact / deploy-pages wiring as the deleted docs.yaml).
